body.p: Reconsideration is respectfully requested. Claims 1-11, 13-16, and 18-20 are pending, of which claims 1, 10, and 13 have been amended without prejudice. Claims 12 and 17 have been canceled without prejudice. No new matter has been introduced. For the reasons set forth below, it is respectfully submitted that the pending claims are allowable.

Claims 1, 10 and 13 were objected to for certain alleged informalities. 1/18/24 NFOA at 2. For the sole purpose of advancing prosecution, and without conceding to the merits of the objections, claim 1 is amended without prejudice to recite the term, "the second processing circuitry," in line 6. Claim 1 is further amended without prejudice to recite the term, "the at least one" in line 9. Claim 10 is amended without prejudice to recite the term, "the sensor fault," in line
9. Claim 13 is amended without prejudice to recite the term, "the sensor fault," in lines 10-11. Accordingly, withdrawal of the objections to claims 1, 10 and 13 is respectfully requested.

Claims 8 and 15 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being allegedly indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter. See 1/18/24 NFOA at 2-3. Specifically, the 1/18/24 NFOA alleges that it is unclear if the term, "analyte level measurements," in claims 8 and 15 is the same or different from the collected data of claim 1 and claim 13. Id. at 3. Applicants respectfully disagree.

It is respectfully submitted that the term, "analyte level measurements," in claims 8 and 15 is different from the collected data of claim 1 and claim 13. Claim 1 recites that "the sensor control device is configured to collect sensor data indicative of an analyte level from the analyte sensor." The specification further describes that the sensor control device 102 collects raw data from the user's body, and then converts the raw data into a form that is representative of the analyte level. See Para. [0035]. Thus, the analyte level measurements recited in claims 8 and 15 cannot be the raw data that is collected by the sensor control device, as recited in claims 1 and 13. As such, it is requested that the Section 112 rejections to claims 8 and 15 be withdrawn.
Claims 1-12 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §101 and section 33(a) of the AIA as being

allegedly directed to or encompassing a human organism. See 1/18/24 NFOA at 3. Specifically, the 1/18/24 NFOA alleges that because claim 1 recites "an analyte sensor at least a portion of which is inserted into a user's body," it improperly claims a human as part of the claimed system. Id.

For the sole purpose of advancing prosecution, and without conceding to the merits of the objections, claim 1 is amended without prejudice to recite, "an analyte sensor at least a portion of which is configured to be inserted into a user's body." Accordingly, withdrawal of the Section 101 rejections to claims 1-12 is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-6, 8-10, 13-16, and 18-19 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as being allegedly anticipated by U.S. Publ. No. 2016/0022221 ("Ou"). See 1/18/24 NFOA at 4-9. Because claim 1 has been amended without prejudice to incorporate the claim limitations of claim 12, and claim 13 has been amended without prejudice to incorporate the claim limitations of claim 17, it is requested that the Section 102 rejection to claims 1 and 13 be withdrawn, as well as to all claims that depend therefrom.

Claim 7 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over Ou in view of W002058537 ("Heller"). See 1/18/24 NFOA at 9-10. Claims 11, 12, 17, and 20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being allegedly unpatentable over Ou in view of U.S. Publ. No. 2016/0296148 ("Hayter"). See 11/8/23 NFOA at 8-15. For the reasons set forth below, it is
respectfully submitted that the cited references, either alone or in combination, fail to disclose all of the limitations of the pending claims.
Independent claims 1 and 13, as amended, recite (with emphasis added):

1. An analyte monitoring system, comprising: a sensor control device including an analyte sensor at least a portion of which is configured to be inserted into a user's body, first processing circuitry, and a first
non-transitory memory, wherein the sensor control device is configured to collect
sensor data indicative of an analyte level from the analyte sensor; and
a reader device comprising a second processing circuitry and a second non- transitory memory,
wherein at least one of the first or the second non-transitory memory includes instructions that, when executed, cause the at least one of the first or the second
processing circuitry to:
calculate a rate of change metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the rate of change metric is calculated at a first time;
calculate a sum of analyte levels metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the sum of analyte levels metric is calculated at a second time;
compare the rate of change metric with a first threshold and compare the sum of analyte levels metric with a second threshold; and
in response to a determination that the rate of change metric exceeds the first threshold, that the sum of analyte levels metric exceeds the second threshold, and
that a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a
predetermined time threshold, generate an indication of a sensor fault.
13. A computer-implemented method for detecting a sensor fault, the method comprising:
collecting, by a sensor control device comprising an analyte sensor at least a portion of which is inserted into a user's body, sensor data indicative of an analyte
level;
calculating a rate of change metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the rate of change metric is calculated at a first time;
calculating a sum of analyte levels metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the sum of analyte levels metric is calculated at a second time;
comparing the rate of change metric with a first threshold and comparing the sum of analyte levels metric with a second threshold; and
in response to determining that the rate of change metric exceeds the first threshold, that the sum of analyte levels metric exceeds the second threshold, and
that a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a
predetermined time threshold, generating an indication of a the sensor fault.

It is respectfully submitted that the cited references, either alone or in combination, fail to disclose the features of amended independent claims 1 and 13. Amended independent claims 1 and 13 have incorporated the limitations of claims 12 and 17, respectively. The 1/18/24 NFOA alleges that these claim limitations are unpatentable over Ou in view of Hayter. 1/18/24 NFOA at 11-12. Applicants respectfully disagree.

Neither Ou nor Hayter discloses the claim limitations of "calculating a rate of change metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the rate of change metric is calculated at a first time," and "calculating a sum of analyte levels metric based on the collected sensor data, wherein the sum of analyte levels metric is calculated at a second time." They also fail to disclose determining whether "a difference between the first time and the second time is less than a predetermined time threshold."
Accordingly, the cited references, either alone or in combination, fail to disclose all of the limitations of independent claims 1 and 13, and it is requested that the Section 103 rejection to claims
1 and 13 be withdrawn, as well as to all claims that depend therefrom.

Amendments to and/or cancellations of the claims are made without prejudice and solely to clarify the issues before the Examiner and/or to advance prosecution of this application and do not constitute a defacto acquiescence to any objection and/or rejection. Accordingly, this response does not concede that previously pending claims are not patentable.

The right is reserved to pursue claims to any subject matter supported by the disclosure of this application in one or more continuation and/or divisional applications at a later time, including the subject matter of any previously pending claims regardless of whether those claims were amended or cancelled herein. This may entail the pursuit of broader claims, narrower claims, and subject matter that was previously relinquished by virtue of argument or amendment.

Any silence with regard to the rejections of and/or objections to certain dependent claims constitutes a recognition that such are moot based on amendments or remarks made with respect to the independent claim from which the dependent claims depend. Such silence does not constitute a defacto acquiescence to any objection and/or rejection.

In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that all claims are in allowable form. In the event that the Examiner deems that a discussion would be helpful in advancing prosecution, the Examiner is invited to call the undersigned at (949) 432-9993. The USPTO is hereby authorized to
charge any outstanding fees to Deposit Account No. 50-5201.
